meeting_header:
Date: 2025-05-06 | Start: 15:00 PDT | Duration: 45 mins
Attendees: Nina Patel (Redwood AE), Carlos Mendes (Redwood SE), Jared Lin (Aurora CTO), Maya Rao (Aurora Head of Data), Sandeep Kaur (Aurora Procurement), Ethan Price (Eng Manager)
summary: Weekly POC closeout: reviewed final performance numbers, tuned model config, validated success criteria for business case, and aligned exec next steps. Customer requested final deliverables (report, cost model, tuned profiles) and will run internal exec sign-off. Procurement has timeline questions; security/regulatory checks passed initial review.
topics: Business case numbers and cost model
Stakeholder alignment and exec sign-off timeline
transcript:
[00:00] Nina Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check — audio ok?
[00:05] Jared Lin: Yep, loud and clear.
[00:08] Carlos Mendes: Good here.
[00:10] Nina: Cool. Agenda — quick run through final POC results, tuning notes, confirm success criteria met, walk through the business case summary, and list next steps for executive sign-off and procurement. We got 45 minutes.
[00:25] Maya Rao: Sounds good. We put time aside to make a decision this week so thanks.
[00:29] Nina: Great. Carlos, can you take us through the numbers?
[00:32] Carlos: Sure. So we ran the final 72-hour run against your customer support workload — synthetic replay from last quarter. Key numbers first: median token latency on the hosted config with standard batching was 110 ms per token, p95 at 230 ms. With the dedicated pool and the tuned batch profile we got median down to 62 ms and p95 120 ms. Throughput increased roughly 2.8x on average.
[01:02] Ethan Price: That's the dedicated numbers, right? The hosted numbers are the 110 ms?
[01:05] Carlos: Correct. The hosted API profile we left conservative for multi-tenant safety. Dedicated runtime used the optimized kernel selection and prefix KV cache; plus we applied the -8 quantization profile on the tails which reduced memory and improved throughput.
[01:22] Jared: Quick question — when you say -8 quantization, is that post-training quant or on-the-fly weights?
[01:27] Carlos: It's static quantization we compile at serving time — not affecting model artifact in your dev repo. We produced two variants: q8-fp (balanced) and q4-fast (more aggressive). For Aurora's NLU intent models we recommend q8-fp to avoid accuracy drift — the delta in rouge/bleu-ish metrics was within 1.2% for q8-fp, q4-fast showed a 4–6% hit on edge cases.
[01:52] Maya: Did you measure hallucination or answer fidelity? Our success criteria included <2% mistaken entity extraction.
[01:58] Carlos: Right — we ran the entity extraction eval set. q8-fp had 0.9% mismatch vs ground truth. Hosted baseline was 0.8% so basically parity. q4-fast rose to 3.5% on rare long-tail prompts.
[02:15] Nina: TLDR: dedicated + q8 gives you the latency and cost profile you targeted while staying inside the success criteria.
[02:22] Jared: That aligns with what we saw in the dashboard. Speaking of cost — can you run through the cost model?
[02:27] Nina: Yeah. We built a simple three-year TCO for the expected production load you shared (avg 120k tokens/day). Hosted estimate is $X/day — sorry placeholder — let me be concrete: hosted model variant estimate is $0.38 per 1k tokens given current rates, translating to about $45k/year. Dedicated reserved capacity with the optimized config brings token cost down to about $0.12 per 1k tokens after amortizing reserved GPUs and OPEX, total about $15k/year for the tokens plus reserved fees. The big delta is the reserved capacity commit and the initial runbook for autoscaling.
[03:05] Sandeep Kaur: Can you put that in a spreadsheet with line items? Procurement needs line items: reserved fee, variable usage, support, ingress/egress.
[03:13] Nina: Absolutely — we'll send the breakout. Carlos, can you attach the token-level CSV?
[03:18] Carlos: Yep, I'll export token-level latency/cost CSV and upload to the shared drive after this call.
[03:22] Sandeep: Also need a single PO line or MSA guidance. What's the timeline for contract?
[03:27] Nina: Typical is MSA + SOW for Dedicated. We can support a month-to-month during ramp but procurement often prefers quarterly commits. We can provide standard enterprise terms, and I'll loop Legal for redlines.
[03:36] Sandeep: Okay, I'll share Aurora's PO template and target May 30 as a soft cut for a PO decision.
[03:41] Maya: Quick note on security — we ran your SOC2 summary with our security team. A few follow-ups but no showstoppers. Data residency — we need logs retained in US only for now. Is that doable on Redwood Private?
[03:55] Carlos: Yes, Private supports region pinning and KMS integration. Auditing logs can be configured to your SIEM; we pushed a sample audit trace earlier. There may be slight differences in observability retention but that is configurable.
[04:07] Jared: Does Private require on-prem infra or you do VPC-hosted in our cloud?
[04:11] Carlos: We offer both: VPC private deployment in your cloud account and an on-prem air-gapped option if needed. For Aurora we recommended VPC in your AWS account to meet residency and minimize ops.
[04:21] Ethan: Latency-wise, VPC will be slightly better than hosted multi-tenant and on par with dedicated depending on placement.
[04:28] Nina: Okay — back to business case: the execs want a one-page summarizing: metrics met, cost delta, and recommended next steps. Jared, do you want us to draft that one-pager or do you prefer internal?
[04:38] Jared: If you can draft it that'd be helpful. We'll annotate then push to the exec review. Include the three-year TCO and risk table — ops, compliance, model drift.
[04:47] Nina: Will do. We'll include a recommended runway: start with dedicated small pool and 30-day phasing, then scale once traffic stabilizes.
[04:55] Maya: Question — fallback behavior if capacity spikes? We saw a couple of timeouts during synthetic load.
[05:00] Carlos: Good catch. We configured automatic fallback to hosted compatible model variant and queuing with shed policy. For the POC we allowed short tail queuing; for production we can set a hard limit and route to the lower-cost q4 variant as a graceful degradation.
[05:15] Jared: Would that affect SLA? I want guaranteed throughput during peak business hours for support triage flows.
[05:21] Nina: We can define an SLO per route; for mission-critical flows you can pin capacity and evict non-critical routes. That's typically part of Dedicated SLA discussion.
[05:30] Sandeep: Pricing for guaranteed SLOs is something we need to include in procurement.
[05:33] Nina: Understood — we'll surface sample SLA language and pricing ranges.
[05:37] Maya: Also, can you confirm the model version pinning process? We need a rollback plan if a release causes regressions.
[05:44] Carlos: Yes — our Console supports version pinning and canary rollouts. You can configure canary at 5–10% traffic with automatic rollback if eval metrics degrade beyond thresholds. We can attach the eval harness we used for the POC so your ML ops team can replay tests before rollout.
[06:02] Ethan: Any sensitivity around PII in logs? We want PII redaction pre-ingest.
[06:07] Carlos: We support pre-ingest filters and token-level redaction. For the POC we masked names on the test corpus but in production we'll help integrate your pre-filter pipeline or deploy Redwood filters in the VPC.
[06:19] Nina: Great. Time check — we have 20 minutes left. Let's confirm success criteria checklist live. Maya, you had sent three green metrics: latency <100 ms median, p95 <250 ms, and entity extraction error <2%. Are we agreeing these passed?
[06:33] Maya: Yes. Median is 62 on dedicated, p95 120; entity error 0.9% per Carlos. So green across the board for the core flows.
[06:42] Jared: From product POV, we want a manual QA signoff on the long-tail prompts. Maya, can you scope an internal verification window — 48 hours?
[06:50] Maya: Yes, we'll run the 48-hour subset and report back by Friday.
[06:54] Nina: Perfect. Action item: Maya to confirm regulatory list and run the 48-hour QA.
[06:59] Maya: I'll do that.
[07:01] Sandeep: On timeline — if exec sign-off happens next week, procurement aims to turn a PO by May 30. Any blockers from Redwood?
[07:09] Nina: No blockers; we'll provide the MSA and SOW templates and the cost workbook. Legal will engage if you want redline support.
[07:17] Jared: One last thing — training for our support agents on failure mode handling. Do you provide runbooks?
[07:22] Carlos: Yes, we'll include runbooks for fallback, monitoring dashboards, and runbook playbooks for latency spikes. We'll also run a 60-min ops workshop during onboarding.
[07:33] Nina: Ok let's recap next steps quickly before we run out of time. Carlos will upload CSV and tuned profiles by Friday; Nina will send final POC report, one-pager and cost model by Friday 2025-05-09; Maya will run 48-hour QA and confirm regulator list; Sandeep will share procurement template and PO timeline; we'll schedule a 30-min exec wrap the week of 2025-05-12.
[07:56] Jared: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[07:58] Nina: Thanks — if nothing else, we'll follow up with the deliverables.
[08:02] Carlos: Thanks.
[08:04] Meeting ends.
